title: WhatsApp AI Chatbot for Business: How It Works, What It Costs and When You Need One
summary: A practical guide to WhatsApp AI chatbots for business: how they work with the WhatsApp Business API, what they can automate (quotes, payments, bookings), costs and how to launch one.
body:
WhatsApp is the main way people talk to businesses in large parts of the world. Clients expect fast answers, often outside business hours. A **WhatsApp AI chatbot** replies instantly, 24/7, and can handle the full journey: answering questions, giving a quote, taking a payment and sending a document.

Here is how it works, what it can do for your business and what to watch out for.

## How a WhatsApp AI chatbot works

A business chatbot runs on the **WhatsApp Business Platform (API)**, not on the regular WhatsApp app. The flow is simple:

1. A client sends a message to your business number.
2. The WhatsApp Business API forwards it to your chatbot.
3. The chatbot understands the request with AI, looks up the right information (prices, availability, client file) and replies.
4. When needed, it sends a payment link, a PDF or hands the conversation to a human.

The best chatbots combine **AI for understanding** with **your own data for answers**. That way, they never invent a price or a policy.

## What a WhatsApp chatbot can automate

- **Answers to frequent questions**: opening hours, prices, delivery, documents required.
- **Quotes**: asking the right questions and calculating an exact price from your rate cards.
- **Payments**: sending a secure payment link by card or mobile money.
- **Bookings and appointments**: proposing slots, confirming and sending reminders.
- **Documents**: generating a contract, invoice, receipt or ticket as a PDF.
- **Lead qualification**: collecting needs and contact details, then creating the lead in your CRM.
- **Follow-ups**: renewal reminders, abandoned quotes, satisfaction surveys.

## Which businesses benefit most

Any business that receives many similar messages: insurance and finance, clinics, schools and training centres, real estate, travel and transport, restaurants, retail and e-commerce, service providers. If your team answers the same ten questions all day, a chatbot pays back quickly.

## Rule-based bot vs. AI chatbot

A **rule-based bot** follows menus ("type 1 for prices"). It is cheap but rigid and frustrating when the client asks something unexpected.

An **AI chatbot** understands free text in many languages and keeps the context of the conversation. Combined with clear rules for prices and actions, it feels natural while staying accurate.

## What it costs

There are three cost blocks:

- **WhatsApp conversation fees** charged by Meta, which depend on the country and the type of conversation.
- **Hosting and AI usage**, usually a small monthly amount.
- **Setup and customisation**: connecting your data, prices, payment provider and brand.

For most small and medium businesses, a chatbot that handles even a fraction of daily messages costs far less than the time it saves.

## Best practices before you launch

- Start with the **top 10 questions** your team receives.
- Connect **real data** (prices, stock, appointments) so answers are always correct.
- Always offer a **human handover**.
- Respect **opt-in rules** and privacy laws in your markets.
- Review conversations every week for the first month to improve answers.
